meta.pageTitle: Bible Study — November 24 | God Doesn't Want You in Hell
meta.title: God Doesn’t Want
meta.footer: Bible Study — November 24  ·  Ordinary Glory: God Doesn’t Want You in Hell  ·  Scripture from the NIV

summary.speaker: Pastor Chris
summary.bigIdea: God does not want anyone in hell, and love, not fear, is what draws us to Jesus and sends us to love others.
summary.overview: Pastor Chris begins with John Avery, a valet at a New York cancer center who encourages every patient he meets. Then he turns to hell. He says that scaring people does not lead them to the real Jesus.

points.title: Love, Not Fear, Draws Us to God
points.text: Dolly Parton said that scared religion is no religion. God takes no pleasure in anyone’s death. He sent his Son to rescue the world, not to condemn it, and perfect love drives out fear.

points.title: Love Calls for Justice and Care
points.text: Hell is real because evil is real, and God’s love for all people means he will judge evil. In the story of the sheep and goats, people who have received God’s love naturally care for those in need.

points.title: The Doors Are Locked From the Inside
points.text: C.S. Lewis described hell as what is left when all a person has is self. A life that is only about me becomes its own hell, and people who trade God for things get what they wished for.

points.title: A Mission of Reconciliation
points.text: The rich man ignored Lazarus at his gate. Need shows that people failed to share, not that God failed. God asks us to receive his love and share it with everyone.

summary.takeaway: This week, tell one person that they are loved and that you believe in them, as John the valet does.

ezek33.text: “Say to them, ‘As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign LORD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that they turn from their ways and live. Turn! Turn from your evil ways! Why will you die, people of Israel?’”

john3.text: “For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through him.”

john4.text: “There is no fear in love. But perfect love drives out fear, because fear has to do with punishment. The one who fears is not made perfect in love.”

matt25.text: “When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, he will sit on his glorious throne. All the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate the people one from another as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. He will put the sheep on his right and the goats on his left. Then the King will say to those on his right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by my Father; take your inheritance, the kingdom prepared for you since the creation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you invited me in, I needed clothes and you clothed me, I was sick and you looked after me, I was in prison and you came to visit me.’”

rom1.text: “For although they knew God, they neither glorified him as God nor gave thanks to him, but their thinking became futile and their foolish hearts were darkened. Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images made to look like a mortal human being and birds and animals and reptiles. Therefore God gave them over in the sinful desires of their hearts to sexual impurity for the degrading of their bodies with one another. They exchanged the truth about God for a lie, and worshiped and served created things rather than the Creator—who is forever praised. Amen.”

luke16.text: “There was a rich man who was dressed in purple and fine linen and lived in luxury every day. At his gate was laid a beggar named Lazarus, covered with sores and longing to eat what fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.”

cor5.text: “All this is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation: that God was reconciling the world to himself in Christ, not counting people’s sins against them. And he has committed to us the message of reconciliation.”

col1.text: “For God was pleased to have all his fullness dwell in him, and through him to reconcile to himself all things, whether things on earth or things in heaven, by making peace through his blood, shed on the cross.”

questions.text: Think of something you do because you love it, not because you must. How does that feel different?
If someone believed God was angry with them, what would you want them to hear first?
Why might it bring comfort to know that God will one day make wrongs right?
What small act of care for a stranger has stayed with you, whether you gave it or received it?
Think of a time you saw someone choose to be right instead of happy. What might have helped them let go?
What everyday things can slowly take the place of what matters most?
What helps a community notice and share with neighbors in need, both near and far?
Think of someone who made you feel believed in. What did they say or do?

prayer.label: Closing Prayer
prayer.text:
Dear God,

Thank you that you do not want anyone to be lost. Thank you for sending Jesus to rescue the world and not to condemn it. Forgive us for any time we used fear to speak about you.

Thank you that your love is the strongest force there is. Help us to trust that you will make wrongs right, and that your love is never defeated.

Show us how to care for people in need, as Jesus asked. Keep us from a life that is only about ourselves, and open our eyes to the neighbors near and far who need what we have.

Thank you for reconciling us to yourself. Help us to receive your love with open hands, and to share it with everyone we meet.

We ask this in the name of Jesus. Amen.
prayer.source: — Based on this week’s study: love over fear, justice and care, the danger of self-centeredness, and the mission of reconciliation.
